signature.name: Red Square
signature.detail: The vast cobblestone heart of Moscow, ringed by the Kremlin, St. Basil's and GUM, and the first place every visitor heads. Come early morning or after dark to dodge the crowds and catch the buildings lit up. It's free and open around the clock; the nearest metro is Okhotny Ryad.

signature.name: Moscow Kremlin
signature.detail: A walled city of cathedrals, palaces and armouries that has been the seat of Russian power for centuries. Buy tickets online and go on a weekday morning; the Armoury Chamber needs a separate timed ticket. Enter from the Alexander Garden side via metro Biblioteka imeni Lenina.

signature.name: St. Basil's Cathedral
signature.detail: The candy-coloured onion domes on Red Square are Russia's most recognisable silhouette. Step inside to see the maze of chapels, and photograph it from the Zaryadye Park side at sunset. Tickets are sold at the door; modest dress is respectful.

signature.name: Lenin's Mausoleum
signature.detail: A starkly modern tomb on Red Square holding the embalmed body of the Soviet founder. It's free but opens only a few short morning hours and closes on some weekdays, so check ahead; no bags, phones or photos inside, and expect a queue.

signature.name: Tretyakov Gallery
signature.detail: The definitive collection of Russian painting, from medieval icons to the Blue Dancers and the great 19th-century masters. Allow at least half a day and book a timed ticket online to skip the line. Metro Tretyakovskaya is right outside.

signature.name: GUM
signature.detail: The elegant 19th-century arcade facing the Kremlin, now a department store with a glass roof and historic cafés. It's a good rain shelter and a classic photo spot; go in the evening when the facade is illuminated. Metro Ploshchad Revolyutsii.

signature.name: Moscow Metro Stations
signature.detail: Moscow's underground palaces — chandeliers, mosaics and marble — are a sight in themselves and the cheapest way to cross the city. Ride the circle line and stop at Komsomolskaya and Novoslobodskaya; avoid rush hour for photos. A single trip costs a few dollars.

signature.name: Bolshoi Theatre
signature.detail: One of the world's great opera and ballet houses, with a gilded auditorium that alone justifies the visit. Book ballet or opera tickets well in advance online, or take a guided backstage tour if performances are sold out. Metro Teatralnaya.

signature.name: Cathedral of Christ the Saviour
signature.detail: A colossal white-and-gold cathedral rebuilt in the 1990s, dominating the Moskva River bank near the Kremlin. Go up to the viewing gallery for river views and dress modestly; entry to the main church is free. Metro Kropotkinskaya.

signature.name: Novodevichy Convent
signature.detail: A serene walled convent with red-and-white towers and a famous cemetery of Russian artists and leaders next door. It's a peaceful half-day away from the centre; combine it with a walk around the pond. Metro Sportivnaya.

food: Casual meal $10-18; mid-range dinner for two $40-70
transport: Metro about $0.70 a ride; taxis and ride-hailing cheap
